subject.title: fix(stream): recover visible content when reasoning_delta straddles an inline code span (closes #96869)

question: Should OpenClaw ever reinterpret `reasoning_content` as visible output based only on unmatched Markdown delimiters, or must recovery require an explicit provider/model compatibility signal?
rationale: The PR trades silent visible-content loss from malformed provider streams against possible disclosure of genuine reasoning from conforming streams; source inspection and tests cannot choose that privacy policy on maintainers' behalf.

options.title: Require explicit compatibility signal
options.body: Preserve reasoning as private by default and enable recovery only for providers or models with a reviewed contract or observed malformed-stream behavior.

options.title: Accept delimiter-based recovery
options.body: Adopt the provider-agnostic heuristic and explicitly own the possibility that genuine reasoning may become visible after unmatched code delimiters.

options.title: Pause this recovery
options.body: Leave the current private-field contract unchanged until a trustworthy classification signal or upstream provider fix exists.

recommendation.title: Require explicit compatibility signal
recommendation.body: Preserve reasoning as private by default and enable recovery only for providers or models with a reviewed contract or observed malformed-stream behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest merged-history signal is the shared partitioner and streaming integration introduced in pull request https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88924.
